title: Pediatric Cardiology, Part 2: Congenital heart defects

sections.title: History and exam in suspected heart disease
notes: Timing: **severe coarctation presents with heart failure in week 1**, large left-to-right shunts at **6 to 8 weeks**.
Maternal diabetes: **hypertrophic cardiomyopathy**. Lithium: **Ebstein anomaly**.
Four-limb pulses and BP, S2 (single or widely split). Not all cyanosis is cardiac: tension pneumothorax.

sections.title: Murmur myths and red flags
notes: Murmur in the first hours can be a **closing ductus** (benign). VSD or AV canal may have **no murmur at birth**. ASD is repaired around school age.
Heart disease mimics sepsis in newborns (coarctation, hypoplastic left heart).
Red flags: **unexplained metabolic acidosis**, poor perfusion, **arm vs leg pulse difference**, **single S2**, loud S2, hyperactive precordium, shock. Call cardiology.

sections.title: Acyanotic left-to-right shunts
notes: **VSD is most common**, then PDA, ASD, AV canal (**trisomy 21**).
Increased pulmonary vascularity on x-ray. Heart failure at **4 to 6 weeks** as pulmonary resistance falls. **Oxygen worsens it**.
Untreated: **Eisenmenger** (early with AV canal, years with ASD).
**Echo every baby with suspected trisomy 21**, murmur or not.

sections.title: Cyanotic defects by lung markings
notes: **Decreased pulmonary markings**: tetralogy of Fallot, tricuspid atresia, Ebstein, pulmonary atresia, Eisenmenger.
**Increased markings**: transposition, TAPVR, truncus arteriosus.

sections.title: Hyperoxia test and prostaglandin
notes: Give **100% oxygen** and check arterial PaO2. Lung disease rises to **100 mmHg or more**. Cardiac stays below 100.
Ductal-dependent lesions: start **prostaglandin E1**. Side effects: **apnea**, flushing.

sections.title: 22q11 deletion screening
notes: Screen any baby with **conotruncal defects** (truncus arteriosus, tetralogy, interrupted aortic arch, pulmonary atresia with VSD), even without DiGeorge features.
Preferred test: **chromosomal microarray**. FISH misses small deletions.

sections.title: Shock or heart failure in week 1
notes: Poor perfusion, metabolic acidosis, hepatomegaly, gallop in the first week: **left-sided obstruction**: **severe coarctation, hypoplastic left heart, interrupted aortic arch**.
**Prostaglandin to open the ductus** and urgent cardiology.

sections.title: Reading the pediatric chest x-ray
notes: Cardiothoracic ratio **over 55% is cardiomegaly**.

Prominent aortic knob: aortic stenosis. Prominent pulmonary artery: left-to-right shunt. Left atrial enlargement: wide carina, double density. Upturned apex: right ventricle. Downward apex: left ventricle.
ASD: big RA, RV, pulmonary artery. Tetralogy: big RV, small pulmonary arteries, **boot-shaped heart**. PDA and VSD: big LA, LV. **Coarctation: rib notching**.

sections.title: X-ray cases
notes: 2-month-old, cardiomegaly, increased markings: **VSD or PDA**.
Cyanotic spells, narrow mediastinum, upturned apex, low markings: **tetralogy of Fallot**.
Cyanosis in the first hours, single loud S2, **egg on a string**, increased markings: **transposition**. Prostaglandin.
Huge heart filling the chest, clear lungs: **Ebstein anomaly**.
**Snowman** heart, recurrent lung infections: **supracardiac TAPVR**.

sections.title: ECG findings
notes: Tall R in V1, deep S in V6, **upright T in V1 after 1 week**: right ventricular hypertrophy (tetralogy, pulmonary hypertension).
**Superior axis (negative aVF)**: **AV canal**, primum ASD, tricuspid atresia.
Right bundle branch block (wide QRS, RSR' in V1): **after heart surgery** (repaired tetralogy), Ebstein, primum ASD.
**WPW**: short PR, wide QRS, **delta wave**.

sections.title: Review: transposition and TAPVR
notes: Transposition: give **prostaglandin first**. Echo is for surgical planning, not an emergency first step.
**Obstructed infradiaphragmatic TAPVR**: severe distress and cyanosis right after birth, looks like RDS or GBS pneumonia. **Surgical emergency**.

sections.title: Heart failure by age
notes: Week 1: **left-sided obstruction** (prostaglandin). 6 to 8 weeks: **left-to-right shunt**. Older child: myocarditis, rheumatic heart disease.

sections.title: Syndromes and heart defects
notes: **Trisomy 21**: AV canal, VSD. **Turner**: **bicuspid aortic valve**, coarctation, lifelong follow-up for dissection. Trisomy 13 and 18: VSD. Noonan: **pulmonary stenosis**.
**Williams**: **supravalvar aortic stenosis**, peripheral pulmonary stenosis, **hypercalcemia**, friendly personality. Holt-Oram: ASD with arm and hand defects.
Lithium: Ebstein. Alcohol: ASD, VSD. Retinoic acid and maternal diabetes: transposition (diabetes also HCM). **Maternal lupus: congenital heart block**.
